title: A non-square element cuts a regular local hypersurface
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] and let $f\in\mathfrak m$. If $f\notin\mathfrak m^2$, then $R/fR$ is a regular local ring.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), used in the proof of More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07PF

mathlib_searches.query: regular local ring f not in maximal ideal squared quotient R/(f) is regular local
mathlib_searches.results: No exact quotient criterion; regular-local and regular-sequence infrastructure only.

mathlib_searches.query: regular local hypersurface quotient by element outside m^2
mathlib_searches.results: IsRegularLocalRing and regular-sequence predicates, but no hypersurface quotient theorem.
RegularLocalRing/Defs.lean and Regular/RegularSequence.lean contain predicates and localization facts; no quotient-by-m^2 criterion.
